parent: Vir Health Limited (Numan is its trading name; company number 11449267). Registered pharmacy: Numan Operations Limited (GPhC 9011408).
model: UK online men's health clinic and pharmacy: an anonymous questionnaire, then the patient picks a subscription product, pays upfront for 3, 6 or 12 months, and a clinician reviews the request after checkout.

access.accountWall: At …/subscribe/hair-loss/<draft id>/profile, after the questionnaire, GP choice, optional email (skippable), product selection, 'what to expect', billing frequency and add-ons. The screen shows the order summary and asks for email, password, legal name, date of birth, phone, sex and delivery address. The full recommendation and all plan prices are visible before it. Direct purchase of Rosemary Oil hits the same form on its first screen.
access.coverageNote: Stage 1 (map). The browser was not blocked. All 29 questions of the live men's questionnaire were reached and saved with every option; the served data also gives the engine result of every option (proceed, reject with message, clinician query with internal note). The baseline man was walked to the account wall twice (main link and Regaine link). One stop screen (under 18) was opened. The product filter was read in the served JavaScript and seen once in an all-flags walk. Not done: one-change tests of most options (stage 2), anything after the account wall, and any women's flow (none exists). robots.txt disallows /subscribe for crawlers; the walks were single, slow, human-style sessions and each consultation start created one anonymous draft on Numan's side (eight confirmed in the network logs, possibly nine).

flows.name: Men's hair-loss consultation (questionnaire 'hair_loss', version 14, revision 'smart')
flows.stagesSummary: Consent screen → 8 to 28 anonymous questions out of a bank of 29 (the baseline man sees 8) → GP-notification choice → optional email (skippable) → product selection (the recommendation) → 'what to expect' → billing frequency → add-ons → ACCOUNT WALL at …/profile (order summary + create account + address) → payment, identity check and clinician review (not tested).

questions.text: The really important bit. By clicking “Next”, you are confirming that you: Are completing this consultation for yourself and to the best of your knowledge. Were assigned male at birth. Will disclose any serious illnesses or operations you have had or any prescription medication you currently take. Will only use one method of hair loss treatment at a time and will not combine more than one different medication for the condition. Are aware that finasteride is associated with depression, suicidal thoughts, and sexual dysfunction including decreased sex drive, erectile dysfunction, and ejaculation problems. These side effects can occur independently of each other and may persist after stopping treatment. A clinician will review your suitability before any prescription is issued. Will answer the questions in the next section about your physical and mental health history honestly, and are aware that your responses are reviewed by a prescribing clinician and kept confidential. Are aware that you should not take finasteride if you’re trying for a baby. Are aware that you may be prescribed an unlicensed treatment. Are accepting our Terms & Conditions and Terms of Sale.

options.label: Next
options.effect: Creates an anonymous draft on Numan's server (POST api.numan.com/v1/subscriptions, status 'draft', questionnaire hair_loss version 14, revision 'smart') and opens the first question. Sex is never asked as a question: being assigned male at birth is asserted here.

questions.purpose: Consent, declaration of male sex at birth, finasteride risk warnings and notice that an unlicensed medicine may be prescribed.
questions.shownWhen: always (entry screen of every hair-loss consultation link)

questions.text: Please tell us your age.

options.label: 65 or over
options.effect: Adds one extra question asking whether he still wants to be considered (see next question). No stop on its own.
Goes on to the hair-loss pattern question.

options.label: Under 18
options.effect: Stops the consultation. Screen 'No suitable treatment': "The safety of our patients is our top priority. Unfortunately, as hair loss under the age of 18 could be a sign of an underlying condition, we’re unable to recommend a hair loss treatment for you. Please contact your doctor for advice." plus an invitation to email clinic@numan.com, a 'Review your answers' button and 'Back to homepage'.

questions.purpose: Age gate. Under-18s are refused; 65 and over get an extra confirmation.
questions.branchDetail: Under 18 stops; 65 or over adds one question.

questions.text: Hair loss products are not guaranteed to show results in individuals over the age of 65, however, there is still a possibility for hair growth to reoccur. Would you still like to be considered for treatments?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: Carries on with the normal questions. No clinician flag in the definition and no change in the engine flags.

options.label: No
options.effect: Stops: "Unfortunately, we’re unable to recommend a hair loss treatment for you. Please contact your doctor for advice." (reject result in the served definition; not clicked).

questions.purpose: Sets expectations for older men and lets them opt out.

questions.text: What kind of hair loss do you have?

options.label: Temples
options.effect: Proceeds. No clinician flag. The served product-selection code does not read this answer, so it should not change which products are shown (not yet tested).

options.label: Temples and Crown
options.effect: Proceeds to the onset question. Baseline answer.

options.label: Moderate
options.effect: Proceeds. No clinician flag in the definition (not yet tested).

options.label: Extensive
options.effect: Proceeds. No clinician flag in the definition (not yet tested).

options.label: Patchy
options.effect: Stops: "Defined circular areas of hair loss on the head may suggest a form of alopecia, therefore it is best to consult your GP so they can investigate." (reject result in the definition).

options.label: Complete
options.effect: Stops: "Our treatments are not effective in individuals who have experienced complete hair loss." (reject result in the definition).

options.label: Other hair loss pattern
options.effect: Adds a free-text question about the hair loss and flags the case for a clinician. Internal note served with the option: finasteride is unlikely to work outside male pattern loss, minoxidil may; prescribing is case by case; the team may send a 'further information needed' message.

questions.purpose: Picture-based pattern check (seven drawings) to confirm male pattern hair loss and screen out patchy or complete loss.
questions.branchDetail: Patchy and Complete stop; Other adds a free-text question and a clinician flag.

questions.text: Please tell us about your hair loss: can you describe the appearance of your hair loss; do you have a diagnosis for your hair loss?; for how long has it occurred?; has anything made it better or worse, such as stress?; do you have any other symptoms?. This information is needed so that our clinicians can ensure the prescription is safe for you to take.
questions.purpose: Free-text description for the clinician when the pattern does not match the drawings.

questions.text: When did you start to notice your hair loss?

options.label: Over the last few days or weeks
options.effect: Stops: "…our treatments are not suitable for you because they are not designed for sudden hair loss. Sudden hair loss can have a number of causes and we recommend you seek advice from your usual GP…" (reject result in the definition).

options.label: My hair loss started gradually over the last few months or years
options.effect: Proceeds to the allergy question.

questions.purpose: Screens out sudden hair loss, which needs a GP.

questions.text: Do you have an allergy or intolerance to any of the following?

options.label: I am allergic to minoxidil
options.effect: Sets the engine flag hasAllergyToMinoxidil (seen in the flags call). The product-selection JS then hides every minoxidil-containing product. Also adds a free-text 'how do you react' question and marks the case for clinician query. Seen only together with other answers so far.

options.label: I am allergic to finasteride
options.effect: Sets hasAllergyToFinasteride. The product-selection JS then hides every finasteride-containing product (tablets, both kits with tablets, and the sprays that contain finasteride). Also adds the free-text reaction question and a clinician query. Seen only together with other answers so far.

options.label: I have a lactose intolerance or allergy
options.effect: Adds the lactose tolerance question (finasteride tablets contain lactose). No flag by itself.

options.label: I am not allergic to any of the above
options.effect: Exclusive option. Proceeds to the scalp question.

questions.purpose: Drug allergy and lactose screen. This is the main automatic product filter.
questions.branchDetail: Minoxidil or finasteride allergy adds a reaction question and removes that drug's products; lactose adds a tolerance question.

questions.text: Please let us know how you react when you take this medicine
questions.purpose: Free-text description of the allergic reaction for the clinician.
questions.shownWhen: minoxidil and/or finasteride allergy ticked (seen with both ticked; not yet separated)

questions.text: Finasteride tablets contain very small amounts of lactose. If you have taken a tablet formulation before without experiencing symptoms, it is unlikely that you will get undesirable effects from the lactose within our tablets.

options.label: I can’t tolerate any amount of lactose and I would like to be considered for non-lactose containing preparations only
options.effect: Flags the case for a clinician. Internal note: confirm the request is for a treatment without lactose; if tablets were requested, contact the patient and offer alternatives. The engine flags did not change, so tablets are not hidden automatically.

options.label: I can tolerate very small amounts of lactose
options.effect: Proceeds, no flag in the definition (not clicked).

questions.purpose: Checks whether trace lactose in finasteride tablets is acceptable.

questions.text: Are you experiencing any of the following symptoms on your scalp?

options.label: Pain, itching, burning or bumps
options.effect: Adds a free-text follow-up and flags the case. Internal note: may be psoriasis, dermatitis or another scalp condition; minoxidil is not suitable unless the patient confirms there is no active condition. When all four scalp options were ticked together the engine set isMinoxidilEligible to false; which option does that is not yet separated.

options.label: Red rinds or rashes
options.effect: Adds a free-text follow-up and flags the case, with the same internal note about minoxidil and active scalp conditions. Part of the combined answer that set isMinoxidilEligible to false.

options.label: Dandruff
options.effect: Adds a follow-up asking whether he still wants topical treatments. No flag by itself in the definition.

options.label: Psoriasis or eczema
options.effect: Adds a free-text follow-up and flags the case. Internal note: minoxidil is not suitable with an active scalp condition such as eczema or psoriasis. Part of the combined answer that set isMinoxidilEligible to false.

options.label: No
options.effect: Exclusive option. Proceeds to 'Are any of the following true?'.

questions.purpose: Scalp-condition screen; active scalp disease is a reason not to use minoxidil.
questions.branchDetail: Each ticked symptom adds its own follow-up; the combined answer switched minoxidil off.

questions.text: You mentioned you have pain, itching, burning or bumps on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing)
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about scalp pain, itching, burning or bumps for the clinician.
questions.shownWhen: scalp: 'Pain, itching, burning or bumps' ticked

questions.text: You mentioned you have red rinds or rashes on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing).
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about red rinds or rashes for the clinician.

questions.text: Topical formulations (such as spray) may worsen dandruff. Would you still like to be considered for topical treatments?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: Proceeds, no flag.

options.label: No
options.effect: Flags the case. Internal note: confirm the request is not for a topical treatment; if it is, contact the patient. Whether topical products are also hidden is not yet tested.

questions.purpose: Warns that sprays may worsen dandruff and asks whether topical treatment is still wanted.

questions.text: You mentioned you have eczema or psoriasis on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing)
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about scalp psoriasis or eczema for the clinician.

questions.text: Are any of the following true?

options.label: I have noticed hair loss on other areas of my body other than my head.
options.effect: Adds a free-text follow-up and flags the case. Internal note: finasteride is unlikely to work in conditions other than male pattern baldness; minoxidil may; decide case by case.

options.label: I am undergoing PSA (prostate) monitoring or I have previously been diagnosed with prostate cancer.
options.effect: Adds the PSA follow-up (must tell his GP he takes finasteride; may opt out of finasteride).

options.label: I have been diagnosed with high or low blood pressure.
options.effect: Adds the blood-pressure follow-up (minoxidil may lower blood pressure further; may opt out of minoxidil).

options.label: I have been diagnosed with asthma.
options.effect: Adds the asthma follow-up (alcohol-based sprays may worsen asthma; may opt out of topical products).

options.label: I plan on trying for a baby in the next 12 weeks.
options.effect: Adds the fertility follow-up (stop finasteride 12 weeks before trying; may opt out of finasteride).

options.label: I have previously experienced, or am currently experiencing, depression, anxiety or panic disorders
options.effect: Starts the mental-health branch: mood-risk question, then who manages the condition, medicines, recent dose changes and suicidal thoughts.

options.label: No - none
options.effect: Exclusive option. Skips all eleven follow-ups and goes to the 'most important' question.

questions.purpose: One screen for six cautions: body hair loss, prostate monitoring or cancer, blood pressure, asthma, trying for a baby, mental health.
questions.branchDetail: Each ticked item opens its own follow-up; 'No - none' skips eleven questions.

questions.text: Please tell us about hair loss in areas other than your head. This information is needed so that our clinicians can ensure the prescription is safe for you to take.
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about hair loss elsewhere on the body.
questions.shownWhen: 'hair loss on other areas of my body' ticked

questions.text: If you wish to be considered for finasteride you must tell your GP that you are taking finasteride so that they can interpret your results accordingly.

options.label: I understand and would like to be considered for finasteride containing preparations.
options.effect: Proceeds; engine flags unchanged.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for finasteride containing preparations.
options.effect: Not yet tested. The definition only says 'proceed' with no clinician flag; by its wording it should rule finasteride products out.

questions.purpose: Tells men under prostate monitoring that finasteride changes PSA results; lets them opt out of finasteride.

questions.text: Taking minoxidil alongside your regular blood pressure medication may cause your blood pressure to decrease further, potentially causing light-headedness, dizziness and fainting.

options.label: I understand that minoxidil may lower my blood pressure and would like to be considered for minoxidil.
options.effect: Proceeds; engine flags unchanged.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for minoxidil.
options.effect: Not yet tested. The definition only says 'proceed'; by its wording it should rule minoxidil products out.

questions.purpose: Warns that minoxidil can lower blood pressure further; lets him opt out of minoxidil.
questions.shownWhen: 'diagnosed with high or low blood pressure' ticked

questions.text: Topical formulations (such as spray) may contain alcohol, inhaling this spray may worsen your asthma symptoms and cause you to become short of breath.

options.label: I understand that topical formulations (such as spray) may worsen my asthma and would like to be considered topical formulations.
options.effect: Proceeds; engine flags unchanged.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for topical formulations (such as spray).
options.effect: Not yet tested. The definition only says 'proceed'; by its wording it should rule the sprays out.

questions.purpose: Warns that alcohol-based sprays can worsen asthma; lets him opt out of topical products.

questions.text: Traces of finasteride have been found in the semen (which could affect the feotus), it is advised to stop taking finasteride 12 weeks prior to trying for a baby.

options.label: I would like to be considered for finasteride and will stop taking finasteride 12 weeks prior to trying for a baby.
options.effect: Proceeds; engine flags unchanged.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for preparations containing finasteride.
options.effect: Not yet tested. The definition only says 'proceed'; by its wording it should rule finasteride products out.

questions.purpose: Fertility warning for finasteride; lets him opt out of finasteride.
questions.shownWhen: 'plan on trying for a baby in the next 12 weeks' ticked

questions.text: Mood alterations including depressed mood, depression and, less frequently, suicidal ideation have been reported in patients treated with finasteride.

options.label: I accept the risk that finasteride can lead to detrimental effects on my mood and would like to be considered for finasteride and/or minoxidil.
options.effect: Continues the mental-health branch (who manages the condition).

options.label: I would like to proceed with a minoxidil only treatment plan.
options.effect: Not yet tested. The definition only says 'proceed'; by its wording it should rule finasteride products out and may skip the rest of the mental-health branch.

questions.purpose: Finasteride mood-risk warning; he accepts the risk or asks for minoxidil only.
questions.branchDetail: Accepting the risk opens the rest of the mental-health branch.

questions.text: Who manages your mental health condition?

options.label: Psychiatrist/Specialist/Consultant
options.effect: The engine flag isFinasterideEligible turned false straight after this answer and turned true again when the answer was changed to GP (runs/s2-men-explore). By the product-selection JS that hides all finasteride-containing products. It also skips the remaining mental-health questions and flags the case. Internal note: the specialist should be informed and confirmation given to Numan before finasteride is started.

options.label: GP
options.effect: Continues: asks which mental-health medicines he takes. Finasteride stays eligible.

questions.purpose: Finds out whether a specialist or the GP manages the condition.
questions.branchDetail: Specialist switches finasteride off and skips the rest of the branch; GP continues.
questions.shownWhen: mood question = accept the finasteride risk

questions.text: What medications do you take for your mental health condition?
questions.purpose: Free-text list of mental-health medicines for the clinician.

questions.text: Have the doses of your medications changed in the last 3 months?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: Adds a free-text list of the changes, flags the case and skips the suicidal-thoughts question. Internal note: a recent dose change suggests the condition may not be stable; the patient should provide a GP letter approving finasteride. Engine flags unchanged.

options.label: No
options.effect: Goes to the suicidal-thoughts question.

questions.purpose: Checks whether the condition is stable.
questions.branchDetail: Yes adds a free-text list and skips the suicidal-thoughts question; No goes to it.
questions.shownWhen: who manages = GP (after the medicines question)

questions.text: Please tell us which medications have been changed, your previous dose and your current dose.
questions.purpose: Free-text detail of the dose changes.
questions.shownWhen: dose changed in the last 3 months = Yes

questions.text: Have you had any suicidal thoughts or feelings of self-harm in the past year?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: Proceeds but flags the case. Internal note: 'Finasteride should not be prescribed for patients with suicidal ideation within the past year… consider them for non-finasteride containing preparations only.' Whether the selection screen also hides finasteride is not yet tested.

options.label: No
options.effect: Proceeds. Internal note: if finasteride is prescribed to anyone with a mental-health history, send the post-approval safety-net message. Engine flags unchanged (runs/s4-men-mentalhealth).

engineSummary: Numan's engine has three layers. (1) A server-driven question tree: the browser asks api.numan.com for one question at a time and each answer returns the next question id. Five answers end the consultation at once (under 18; patchy loss; complete loss; sudden onset; and 'No' from a man of 65 or over). (2) A small set of engine flags computed on the server after every answer (finasteride eligible, minoxidil eligible, allergy to each). The selection screen hides every product containing a drug that is ruled out and then features one product: the three-part kit by default, the product named in the entry link if there was one, otherwise the first product left. The patient can always open the full list and choose something else, and a cosmetic oil is always left even when both drugs are ruled out. (3) Many answers do not change the screen at all: they attach a 'query clinically' note, with written instructions, for the clinician who reviews the order after checkout. Pattern severity, the preference question and age over 65 do not appear to change the offer.
strengths: Short for a healthy man: 8 questions and no account needed to see the recommendation and every plan price.
Safety logic is concentrated in a few clear gates plus clinician notes, including a detailed mental-health branch before finasteride.
Wide range in one flow: licensed tablets, a licensed brand, two unlicensed sprays, three kits, plus a cosmetic and a supplement as fallbacks and add-ons.
180-day money-back guarantee shown on the recommendation and billing screens.
weaknesses: No service for women's hair loss: sex is asserted on a consent screen rather than asked, and every medicine is male-only.

No question about previous hair-loss treatment, sexual side-effect history, heart disease by name, or family history in the current questionnaire (older versions in the app bundle did ask about previous treatment).
The patient, not the engine, chooses the product; the default is always the most expensive kit, and six-monthly prepayment is pre-selected.

Public pages disagree with each other: the prescribing-process page says 'We do not supply unlicensed or unproven treatments' while the consent screen and help centre say the 6% and combination sprays are unlicensed. The first-order banner says 50% off but the pricing call applied 40% (capped at £40) to hair-loss medicines.
When both drugs are ruled out the screen still sells Rosemary Oil with the badge 'Most effective' instead of explaining that no medicine is suitable.
opportunities: A proper women's pathway (the site has women's health but no female hair-loss consultation).
A recommendation that actually uses pattern, severity and stated preferences instead of one default kit.
Clear, consistent wording on licensed versus unlicensed products and on what the first-order discount really is.
Monthly or low-commitment plans made visible: the flow only shows quarterly, six-monthly and annual billing.

limitations: Nothing after the account wall was tested: payment, identity check, any follow-up questions from clinicians, and what is finally prescribed are known only from public pages and app text.
Most option effects come from the definition the site served (code), not from separate replays; options marked 'unknown' have not been tested at all.
The engine flags are calculated on Numan's server. Only their values were seen, not the rules that set them.

Prices were read on 23 Nov 2026 with the first-order code that the site's own links carry; several pricing experiments are named in the app bundle (hl_6_months_promo, hl_price_per_day, HL_ps_science), so another visitor may see different presentation.
Six-monthly and annual prices for products other than the three-part kit and Regaine are worked out from the variant data in the API, not seen on a billing screen.
Who compounds the unlicensed sprays is not stated in any public source found.
